title: Cheap config safeguards and eval budgets (draft)
body:
Purpose:
This is a working draft for attaching explicit safety checks (quality gates) to cheaper inference configurations (e.g., aggressive quant, small-context variants, lower top_k sampling) and for sizing an eval/monitoring budget that catches regressions before customer impact. The goal is an actionable spreadsheet + rollout checklist we can hand to runtime and rollout teams.

Audience:
- Product owners for Redwood Optimize
- Serving/runtime engineers implementing config fallbacks
- SRE + Observability for alerts and dashboards
- Solutions/CS for customer-facing risk communication

High-level approach (summary):
1) Define a small set of candidate "cheap configs" (C1..C4) with estimated cost savings and expected quality delta.
2) Compute per-customer and global expected savings using traffic and token distributions.
3) For each config define two gating signals: offline eval delta and online canary regression metric(s).
4) Map thresholds to automatic actions: allow, limited canary, block, or rollback to baseline.
5) Allocate an eval/monitoring token budget and a cadence for continuous re-eval.

Definitions and primitives (keep simple):
- baseline_config: the default production model/precision for this workload (e.g., fp16-32k).
- cheap_config: any config expected to reduce per-token cost by >= X% (examples below).
- eval_score: a scalar quality metric (e.g., normalized helpfulness score or task-specific metric).
- eval_delta = eval_score(cheap) - eval_score(baseline) (negative means quality drop).
- regression_risk: estimated probability that observed eval_delta will cause customer-visible errors (heuristic).
- monitoring_budget_tokens: tokens reserved each week for synthetic eval and fast regression checks.

Suggested spreadsheet layout (columns we use in our modeling):
- config_id (string)
- description (string) e.g., 4-bit q4_0 + prune 10% prefix cache
- cost_saving_pct (numeric string) e.g., "32%"
- avg_token_cost_usd_per_1k (numeric string) e.g., "0.28"
- latency_p95_ms (numeric string) e.g., "230"
- expected_eval_delta (numeric string) e.g., "-0.06" (normalized)
- eval_metric (string) e.g., "answer_f1" or "avg_helpfulness"
- gating_threshold (numeric string) e.g., "-0.03"
- canary_traffic_pct (numeric string) e.g., "1%"
- canary_duration_hours (numeric string) e.g., "48"
- rollback_action (string) e.g., "auto-rollback"
- monitoring_queries_needed_per_day (numeric string) e.g., "250"
- expected_monthly_savings_usd (numeric string)
- notes (string)

Key formulas (to encode in spreadsheet):
- expected_monthly_savings = baseline_monthly_cost * cost_saving_pct
- baseline_monthly_cost = total_monthly_tokens / 1000 * baseline_token_price
- monitoring_cost = monitoring_budget_tokens / 1000 * avg_token_cost_for_tests
- required_monitoring_queries = ceil((regression_detection_power_target * variance_factor) / |eval_delta|) -- (heuristic, see notes)

Example config rows (quick, synthetic numbers):
- C1: "q4_0, no pruning" | cost_saving_pct=18% | avg_token_cost=0.32 | latency_p95=210ms | expected_eval_delta=-0.01 | gating_threshold=-0.02 | canary=0.5% for 24h | monthly_savings=6,400 USD
- C2: "q4_1 + 50% KV cache pruning" | cost_saving_pct=31% | avg_token_cost=0.24 | latency_p95=260ms | expected_eval_delta=-0.06 | gating_threshold=-0.03 | canary=1% for 72h | monthly_savings=11,200 USD
- C3: "small-context (8k)->reduce sequence" | cost_saving_pct=24% | avg_token_cost=0.26 | latency_p95=195ms | expected_eval_delta=-0.08 | gating_threshold=-0.05 | canary=2% for 72h | monthly_savings=8,900 USD

Notes on the numbers: these are intentionally approximate; we use historical eval variance to choose gating_threshold ~= half the expected_eval_delta magnitude for conservative configs. If expected_eval_delta is small (|delta| < 0.02) we lean on online monitoring instead of blocking.

Quality gate decision logic (pseudocode):
- if offline_eval_delta >= gating_threshold_allow: allow config in self-serve for non-SLA customers
- else if gating_threshold_block <= offline_eval_delta < gating_threshold_allow: require canary rollout + extra monitoring_budget
- else if offline_eval_delta < gating_threshold_block: block config for all customers or require manual approval

Concrete thresholds proposal (initial):
- gating_threshold_allow = -0.015 (<=1.5% normalized drop allowed automatically)
- gating_threshold_block = -0.05 (>=5% drop triggers block/manual approval)
- intermediate zone: require canary and live-synthetic checks (2x monitoring budget)

Canary sizing guidance (heuristics):
- Default canary traffic: min(2% of global traffic, max 5%) for 48–72h if in intermediate zone.
- For high-SLA customers reduce maximum canary to 0.5% or run per-customer explicit opt-in.
- Canary traffic formula suggestion: canary_pct = clamp(0.005, 0.02 * sqrt(customer_monthly_tokens / 1e8), 0.05)

Online monitoring signals to instrument (minimum):
- synthetic evals run every 15m against canonical prompt set (N=200 queries/day baseline)
- production user-level rollback signal: % of requests with short-circuit errors, confidence fallback, or hallucination proxy > X
- latency tail regressions (p95 increase > 30% over baseline)
- downstream user metrics (if available): percent of completions with explicit negative feedback, CS tickets trend

Alerting and automatic actions (playbook):
- If synthetic eval delta exceeds gating_threshold_block => auto-disable config + page oncall
- If synthetic eval delta in intermediate zone for > 6h => escalate to SRE + lengthen canary and double synthetic eval frequency
- If latency_p95 > baseline_p95 * 1.5 for > 15 minutes => rollback and throttle new canaries
- If automated rollback happens, create a retrospective ticket and run a targeted offline eval against the failing prompt slice

Monitoring/eval budget math (example):
Inputs: global_daily_requests=12M, avg_tokens_per_request=120, baseline_token_cost=0.40 per 1k tokens
- baseline_daily_cost = 12,000,000 * 120 / 1000 * 0.40 = $576,000/day (toy example; scale down for product)
- If we plan to test C2 across synthetic sets daily with 1k queries of avg 150 tokens: monitoring_tokens_per_day = 150k tokens
- monitoring_cost_per_day = 150k / 1000 * 0.24 = $36/day -> ~ $1,080/month for continuous daily checks per config
- For N configs and multiple metric slices multiply accordingly; set a global monitoring_budget and cap by ROI (monthly_savings / monitoring_cost should be >= 10x as a rule of thumb)

Risk register (short):
- False negatives: small offline deltas that manifest only in long-tail user prompts. Mitigation: keep a long-tail synthetic set and periodic targeted slices.
- Metric mismatch: synthetic eval not correlated to customer satisfaction. Mitigation: map synthetic metrics to a customer-impact proxy and reweight over time.
- Ops churn: too many configs require SRE time. Mitigation: hard cap of 3 active canaries per week per region.

Open questions to resolve in next iteration:
- How to set per-customer tolerance automatically? default thresholds may be too coarse. (Action: propose per-customer SLA tiers.)
- What is the canonical eval metric? one global scalar or per-workload metric? (Action: product+research to define mapping table.)
- How to share savings with sales/finance for discounts tied to degraded-config opt-ins? (Action: finance to propose revenue-sharing model.)

Next steps (near term):
- [Sofia] finalize spreadsheet template with column types and sample formula cells (due 2024-12-09).
- [Ravi] run a batch offline eval on historical prompt sets for C1..C3 and upload results (due 2024-12-06).
- [Hannah] prototype synthetic eval runner in observability sandbox and measure variance (due 2024-12-13).
- Product/Legal to draft customer-facing language for "opt into cost-savings" offering (due 2024-12-20).

Appendix: Quick checklist for runtime implementers:
- Ensure config metadata includes: expected_cost_saving_pct, offline_eval_score, gating_threshold, canary_limits, rollback_policy_id.
- Instrument synthetic eval endpoint with labels: config_id, canary_run_id, metric_version.
- Emit sampling trace for first-failed request during canary to aid triage.

Rough references and related docs:
- Confluence: Optimize guardrails (linked above)
- Spreadsheet prototype: jira:OPT-2103 contains a pointer to a sheet in the linked artifact
- Prior experiments: see github/ops-playbooks PR 72 for monitoring runner code sample

Notes to self (embellished, informal):
- Keep the model architecture/quantization naming consistent with model-onboarding to avoid confusion.
- For early launches use conservative thresholds; we can relax once we see stable real-world correlation.
- Remember to capture cost-per-customer not just global savings; sales will ask for cohort-level numbers.
